title: WPSS/750/2012 of DEEPAK KUMAR SHARMA Vs JUDGE FAMILY COURT HARIDWAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. (S/S) 750 of 2012
Deepak Kumar Sharma Ö.Petitioner
Versus
Judge, Family Court, Haridwar ...Respondent
Present: Mr. Kuldeep Singh Rawal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate for the respondent.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner is a Class IV employee in the Judge,
Family Court, Haridwar. It is an admitted fact that the
petitioner was appointed on 29.6.2009. According to the
petitioner, he has successfully completed his period of
probation after two years i.e. on 28.6.2011, although no letter
of confirmation was issued by the appointing authority in his
favour. Thereafter vide order dated 1.6.2012 his services have
been terminated. There are two orders which the petitioner
has annexed. The first order is a simplicitor order which says
that the petitioner is a probationer and his services are no
more required and hence his services are being terminated.
There is another order attached with the order dated
1.6.2012 which is a detail order which leads various charges
of negligence and indiscipline against the petitioner. An
inquiry was done against the petitioner and in the enquiry, it
was found that the petitioner has also misplaced the court
file. Thereafter, there was a charge of indiscipline to which
the petitioner was severely warned in the past but no sign of
improvement and if such indiscipline person is kept in the
court, it will give a wrong impression about the judgeship.
Aggrieved the petitioner has filed the present writ petition
before this Court.
2. Although the petitioner specifically contends that the
probation period of two year has already come to an end and

2
he cannot be treated as probationer, counsel for the
respondent Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, on the other hand,
contends that under rule 4 of the Uttaranchal State
Government Servants Confirmation Rules, 2002 an order of
confirmation has to be passed and since this has not been
passed in the case of the petitioner he will be deemed to be
under probation. Admittedly there is no order confirming the
services of the petitioner on record. Consequently, the
petitioner will be deemed to be still a probationer.
3. Now what this Court has to see is whether the
termination order is a simplicitor order and the charges
against the petitioner are the very foundation for terminating
the services of the petitioner. On perusal of the detail order
annexed with impugned order dated 1.6.2012 which has also
been given to the petitioner, it suggest that some kind of
enquiry was conducted by the respondents in which they
came to the conclusion that the petitioner has misplaced the
court file on which his increment was also stopped on
20.10.2011. There are other charges against the petitioner
such as on 18.2.2011 when the petitioner was posted as
Chawkidar at Civil Court, Laksar the lock of Nazarath was
found opened and he also misbehaved with the Presiding
Officer. Thereafter in November, 2011 petitioner refused to
work as Class IV employee etc. Consequently, holding that
the petitioner is a probationer and looking at his past
conduct and concluding that there is no scope for
improvement in the conduct of the petitioner, his services
have been terminated. While in the detail order annexed with
the impugned order dated 1.6.2012 a judgment of the Honíble
Supreme Court passed in State of Uttar Pradesh v.
Rajendra Kumar Singh; (1997) 10 SCC 682 has also been
referred to.

3
4. Although the petitioner may be still under probation,
the foundation of passing of the termination order is the past
conduct of the petitioner and according to the respondents,
petitioner is highly indiscipline and various circumstances
have been cited where it has alleged that the petitioner
indulged in indisciplinary activities. This order is clearly a
stigmatic order. Had the respondents passed an order
simplicitor terminating the services of the petitioner there
would have been no occasion for interfering with the matter
and no interference could have been made by this Court but
once it is clearly established by the petitioner that it was the
alleged indiscipline act of the petitioner for terminating his
services where no opportunity of hearing and show cause
notice was given to him, the order being clearly stigmatic and
is in violation of principle of natural justice and fair play. This
is infact the settled position of law since the 1958 decision of
the Honíble Apex Court in Parshotam Lal Dhingra Vs. Union
of India reported in AIR 1958 SC 36 (V 45 C 6). Therefore,
the writ petition is allowed. Order dated 1.6.2012 is hereby
quashed.
5. However, having said this, since there are serious
charges against the petitioner, respondents are at liberty to
initiate disciplinary proceeding against the petitioner and
take action in accordance with law. It is made clear that till
such a disciplinary proceeding is initiated and thereafter
action is taken against the petitioner, though the order of
termination dated 1.6.2012 is quashed, the petitioner will be
treated to be under suspension.
6. No order as to costs.
 .
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J)
10.7.2013
Kuldeep
